## Memo — week ending 2026-08-10

**Procedural note.** Both LIVING MEMORY sections were present and were read as canonical; nothing reported missing. Six web searches were run before the tool budget was exhausted; two planned queries (Einarsson docket; the Swiss judgment numbers) did not fire, and are reported below as unrun rather than as nulls.

### 1. Item 1 — China's RDP Measures: the regime is now a *grantable, refusable, terminable* entitlement, and that changes the Kim analysis

The record already carries the May 15 2026 Measures, the six-year ceiling and the June 5 2026 transitional-waiver closure. Four things in this week's item are not in the record.

**(a) The tier is 6/4/3, keyed to NMPA registration category.** Jones Day: six years for innovative drugs (Category 1) and overseas-marketed originator drugs first launched domestically (Cat. 5.1 chemical / 3.1 biologic); four years for improved drugs; three years for first-to-file generics of overseas-marketed but domestically unavailable originators (https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2026/05/chinas-new-regulatory-data-protection-regime-becomes-effective-immediately). Note a live discrepancy between practitioner accounts: Ropes & Gray's earlier viewpoint describes improved new drugs (Cat. 2) at **three** years, not four (https://www.ropesgray.com/en/insights/viewpoints/102k744/china-formalizes-regulatory-data-protection-mechanism), and Marks & Clerk reports four with a six-year uplift where a modified drug carries a globally new indication (https://www.marks-clerk.com/insights/latest-insights/102n0rt-strengthening-innovation-china-s-new-era-of-drug-regulatory-data-protection/).
